title: Which City After Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Pick the second city by the clock, not the map.** From Berlin Hauptbahnhof the fast lines run north-west to Hamburg, south through Leipzig and Erfurt to Munich, and west to Hanover. East towards Poland the same distance takes about twice as long.
**Under two hours each way is a day trip.** Wittenberg is 40 minutes, Leipzig 1h15, Hanover 1h35, Erfurt 1h35 and Dresden 1h40. You keep the same hotel and your Berlin evening.

**Hamburg at 1h50 is the strongest second city for most visitors.** The Speicherstadt has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2015 and the harbour makes it feel like a different country. Give it two nights, not one.
**The Baltic needs three or four nights.** Stralsund is 2h35 and a UNESCO old town on the way to Rügen. Rostock is 2h20 and pairs brick gothic with the Warnemünde beach.

**East is slower than it looks.** Szczecin is about 2h30 despite being closer than Hamburg, because the line is being rebuilt and a bus bridge fills the Angermünde gap until 12 December 2026. Poznań is about 2h50, Görlitz 2h55, Wrocław 4h15 and Warsaw 5h25.
**Munich, Cologne and Frankfurt are four-hour cities.** Munich is 4h05, Cologne 4h10 and Frankfurt 3h50, all direct on the ICE. Below three nights the train eats the trip.
**Saver fares open months ahead and lock you to one train.** The flexible fare bought on the day costs far more for the same seat, so book long rides as soon as your Berlin dates are fixed.
**The Deutschlandticket does not cover ICE, IC or EC trains.** It works for the regional run to Wittenberg and not for the fast line to Munich.
**With five days, give Berlin three.** Then either take two nights in Hamburg, or stay put and do Leipzig and Wittenberg as day trips from the same bed.
